hook_line: ISRO TEST-FIRES GSLV CRYOGENIC ENGINE FOR 200 SECONDS AHEAD OF NVS-04 LAUNCH

hook_stat.sub: Flight acceptance hot test of the CE-7.5 cryogenic engine on November 5

stats.label: Kilonewtons of thrust the CE-7.5 produces in vacuum
Fourth satellite in India's second-generation NavIC series, to fly on GSLV-F19

diaspora_bullets: NavIC provides positioning services over India and a region extending about 1,500 km beyond its borders
NVS-04 follows the October 30 launch of NVS-03
news_summary: ISRO completed a 200-second flight acceptance hot test of the CE-7.5 cryogenic engine on November 5 at Mahendragiri, and the engine will now be fitted into the cryogenic stage of GSLV-F19 to launch the NVS-04 navigation satellite.
payoff: With the test complete, the engine will now be inducted into the cryogenic stage of the GSLV-F19 launch vehicle.
